claims.claim: Athanasius was the Patriarch (bishop) of Alexandria.
Athanasius was born c. 296 and died on May 2, 373.
The Synodal Letter to the Bishops of Africa was written after the accession of Damasus to the Roman see in 366, probably between 368 and 372.
The letter is dated 369 in one source.
The letter was written by ninety bishops of Egypt and Libya, including Athanasius.
The letter was addressed to the bishops of Africa.

The principal occasion of the letter was to counteract efforts in the West, especially in Africa, to represent the Council of Ariminum as a final settlement of the Faith and so set aside the authority of the Nicene definition.
A second object was to address the situation of Auxentius, the Arian bishop of Milan, who was still undisturbed in his see while working to spread Arianism.
The letter warns against those attempting to cite the synod of Ariminum against the Council of Nicaea.
The letter defends the Nicene use of the term homoousios (coessential) and explains the reasons for its adoption.
The letter insists that the Nicene Creed implies the Godhead of the Holy Spirit.
The letter refers to letters written by Damasus, bishop of Rome, and synods held in Gaul and Italy concerning the sound Faith.
